message: In the concealed under-deck support frame (C2), the bolted cross-frame connection for the added Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) mass has unproven peak and fatigue demand, Manager. To check it I used hand verification of the static weight calculation (E9) by my repeated check calculation (E10) because connection safety needed independent verification, combined with spring force from the optimal TMD sizing (E4) times stroke from the controlled-response stroke estimate (E6). I found 3924 Newtons static plus about 449 Newtons dynamic for about 4373 Newtons peak per 400 kilogram unit giving about 7 megapascals per bolt in four Metric 16 millimetre bolt (M16) groups well below fatigue limit, according to Den Hartog, 1934 and Eurocode 3, 2005. I propose four Metric 16 millimetre bolt (M16) per 200 kilogram module on galvanized cross-frames with preloaded detail and under-soffit lockable hatches. My position: not ready because Structural Dynamics Lead must confirm girder fatigue review. In the deck-view preservation detail, the deck surface and parapet voids have risk of visual intrusion from fixings or covers, Vibration Control Specialist. To check it I used visibility review of the concealed mounting cross-section (E7) building on the side-view mode-shape layout (E3) with robustness from the detuned damping estimate (E8). I found zero change above deck level with all hardware below soffit clearing 12 millimetres stroke within 30 millimetres clearance, according to French Assessment Service for Roads and Motorways (Setra), 2006. I propose soffit-matched finish with no penetration of wearing surface and concealed routing below. My position: not ready
